shadow.$description: First shadow/elevation tokens in this system — scoped deliberately to floating/overlay UI (Popover, Tooltip, Drawer, Modal), not general surfaces. Every other surface (Input/Select/Search fields, Card) draws separation with a border.default hairline; a shadow is warranted here specifically because these genuinely float above arbitrary page content and need to read as 'lifted', which a border alone doesn't convey. Color reuses the same rgba(21, 25, 30, ...) base as surface.overlay's scrim (semantic/color.tokens.json) — that token's own $description already calls it 'the one legitimate opacity use in this system'; shadows are the second, same reasoning (must composite over arbitrary content, not a known surface). Three steps, matching the three floating contexts, not a general-purpose elevation scale to reach for elsewhere.

sm.$description: Popover/Tooltip — small floating panels anchored to a trigger, need the least visual weight.

md.$description: Drawer — a full-height edge panel, one step more prominent than Popover/Tooltip.

lg.$description: Modal — the most prominent floating surface (paired with its own dedicated overlay scrim, unlike Popover/Tooltip/Drawer), gets the strongest shadow. Small negative spread keeps a 24px blur from reading as a diffuse haze at close range.
